words-only.why:
I checked each of the verifier's four PASS/FAIL pairs against its expect line, and the criterion holds for all of them.

- **Check 1** tests only what the words require: that padLeft is exported, pads on the left with the given fill, falls back to a space when no fill is given, and reaches width characters ("xx7", "00042", "  ab").
- **Check 2** tests only that inputs of equal length and longer come back unchanged.
- **Check 3** requires each exported function to have "its own section… a heading that names the function, with text under it." That is a fair reading of "section", not a stricter test, and it leaves heading style open. Naming padLeft follows from line 1.
- **Check 4** requires only that npm test passes.

The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)": whether padLeft tests were added, how a multi-character fill behaves, whether headings match the `## name(args)` style, and whether the README mentions the default fill.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the five tracked files and the `"test":"node --test"` script. `npm test` exists, and README.md, index.js and test/strutil.test.js are all tracked. The builder's `node -e "import('./index.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m)))"` is valid: a dynamic import inside `-e` resolves relative to the current directory. The verifier's three `node --input-type=module -e "import ... from './index.js'; ..."` commands are valid ESM eval scripts. Their single-quoted JS strings sit safely inside double-quoted shell strings, and they use no `!` or `$` that bash would expand. The `.filter(k=>typeof m[k]==='function')` arrow and the `JSON.stringify` calls are valid JS. `grep -n '^#' README.md` is valid. All arguments fit their programs, and padLeft is created by the builder before it is checked.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items and the briefs handle each one. (1) Builder step 3 says "Right now slugify has no section, so add one. Add `## slugify(s)`" and also asks for a `## padLeft(s, width, fill)` section. (2) Verifier Check 3 lists the exported functions at the head. Its PASS condition requires "at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft" to have sections. It FAILs if "any exported function has no README.md section" and says a PR that adds only padLeft fails. (3) Verifier Check 1 calls `m.padLeft('ab',4)` with no fill argument and expects `"  ab"`, so it checks that the default fill is a space. Nothing in either brief undoes these points.

avoids-must-not.why: Neither must_not item shows up in either brief. Item 1: verifier Check 3 lists the exported functions and passes only when "every function in the list (at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft) has its own section". It also says outright that "a PR that adds only padLeft fails this check", so a README with only a padLeft section can't pass. Item 2: Check 1 uses a one-character fill ('7',3,'x') and fails only on wrong results. It never requires the fill to be one character or checks the parameter count. Check 3 asks for "a heading that names the function, with text under it", which is just what a section is, not a fixed README layout. The `## name(args)` heading style and the multi-character fill behaviour appear only as advisory notes, outside PASS/FAIL. The builder brief's style and test instructions are build guidance, not verification conditions.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief's examples and commands with the verifier brief's probes, and they overlap. Builder step 1 gives "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'". Verifier Check 1 runs exactly those inputs and expects "00042" and "  ab". Builder step 2 gives "padLeft('abcde', 5, '0') === 'abcde' and padLeft('abcdef', 3) === 'abcdef'", the same inputs and expected outputs as verifier Check 2. Builder step 5 also suggests listing the exports with `node -e "import('./index.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m)))"`, which is basically verifier Check 3's probe and isn't a repository test or a command the issue names. It also tells the builder that slugify has no README section, which matches the note in Check 3's FAIL condition. So the builder is handed the checker's own probes, and the criterion breaks.
